key_insight: SegWithU reframes uncertainty as a ‘perturbation energy’ predicted by a lightweight post-hoc head on a frozen segmentation backbone, enabling accurate failure ranking in one forward pass without expensive repeated inference.
problem_solved: Reduces the cost and latency of reliable uncertainty estimation for medical image segmentation by avoiding repeated stochastic inference while improving the practical detection of risky/failed predictions.
method: Post-hoc design: attach a small uncertainty head to a frozen pretrained segmentation backbone so the segmentation model need not be retrained.
Uncertainty-as-perturbation-energy: the head predicts a scalar field that estimates how much input perturbation would change the segmentation (higher energy → higher risk/uncertainty).
Single-forward-pass risk scoring: combine predicted perturbation energy with segmentation outputs to rank and flag likely failures for downstream review or automated safeguards.
impact: Provides a practical, low-latency way to equip deployed segmentation models with reliable uncertainty signals, improving safety and triage in clinical pipelines without high compute overhead.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: frozen segmentation backbone + lightweight uncertainty head (single forward pass)
Illustration of perturbation-energy concept: small input perturbations producing segmentation changes, mapped to an uncertainty heatmap
Comparison chart: failure-ranking performance and runtime of SegWithU vs. multi-sample methods (e.g., MC dropout) and existing single-pass baselines
Workflow icon strip: model inference → uncertainty heatmap → triage/flagging → clinician review
paper_title: SegWithU: Uncertainty as Perturbation Energy for Single-Forward-Pass Risk-Aware Medical Image Segmentation
paper_authors: Tianhao Fu, Austin Wang, Charles Chen, Roby Aldave-Garza, Yucheng Chen
